approachQuestion.prompt:
A Fixed Inventory Request

There are d named item types. Type i has integer unit cost cost[i] and at most cap[i] available copies. Return every integer vector x with 0<=x[i]<=cap[i] and sum(cost[i]*x[i])=T, once. Different types remain distinct even if costs are equal. Output vectors are in input type order.

Examples:
cost=[2,3], cap=[2,2], T=6 -> [[0,2]].
cost=[1,1], cap=[1,1], T=1 -> [[0,1],[1,0]].
cost=[2], cap=[3], T=0 -> [[0]].

Constraints: 1 <= d <= 12; 1 <= cost[i] <= 20; 0 <= cap[i] <= 5; 0 <= T <= 1200. Input arrays must not be modified.

options.text: Process one named type per level and try each allowed copy count. Reject a state if its remaining amount is negative or greater than the entire remaining inventory’s value. Emit a full vector only after all types.
options.feedback: The interval from zero through the suffix maximum contains every possible suffix sum; being outside it proves failure. Equal costs do not merge distinct named types.

options.text: Stop and emit the current vector immediately when the running total first reaches T, without processing later types.
options.feedback: For cost=[2,3], cap=[1,1], T=2, the required result is the full vector [1,0]; a partial vector [1] does not meet the output contract.

options.text: Merge types with equal costs into one capacity and return counts only for the merged types.
options.feedback: For cost=[1,1], cap=[1,1], T=1, the two named-type vectors are distinct and must both remain representable.

options.text: Use the same count-vector search but skip both remaining-amount checks until a full vector has been formed.
options.feedback: This is correct, but explores entire suffixes when even taking every remaining copy cannot reach T or when the total is already too large.

feedback.reason: The interval from zero through the suffix maximum contains every possible suffix sum; being outside it proves failure. Equal costs do not merge distinct named types.
details: Precompute suffix maxima max[i]=sum(cost[j]*cap[j]) for j>=i. At state (i,remaining), return immediately if remaining<0 or remaining>max[i]. If i=d emit only at remaining zero. Otherwise try every count 0..cap[i], store it, recurse to i+1 with reduced remainder, and restore the count.

The suffix capacity bound is an upper limit on what remaining types can supply. Reject remainders above it or below zero, then enumerate legal counts per type. Cost equality alone is insufficient if a chosen count exceeds its cap.

“Process one named type per level and try each allowed copy count. Reject a state if its remaining amount is negative or greater than the entire remaining inventory’s value. Emit a full vector only after all types.”: The interval from zero through the suffix maximum contains every possible suffix sum; being outside it proves failure. Equal costs do not merge distinct named types.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-20-search` only. Let V be the actual recursive-call count including immediately pruned calls, and R count copied vector entries. A call has at most six child counts because capacities are at most five. Build a d+1 suffix array and use one d-entry count vector. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(d + V + R) time, O(d) auxiliary space
O(d + R) time, O(d) auxiliary space
O(d·V + R) time, O(d) auxiliary space
O(d + V + R) time, O(V) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Suffix preprocessing plus bounded per-state count trials and output vectors determines work.
details: Suffix preprocessing costs d. Every call performs bounded count-loop work and constant-time bound checks; output vector copying adds R.
The suffix table, current vector and stack have linear size in the number of types.

Let V be the actual recursive-call count including immediately pruned calls, and R count copied vector entries. A call has at most six child counts because capacities are at most five. Build a d+1 suffix array and use one d-entry count vector.
“O(d + R) time, O(d) auxiliary space”: An amount within suffix bounds is not necessarily attainable; many prefixes may still be searched.
“O(d·V + R) time, O(d) auxiliary space”: Suffix maxima are precomputed and counts per type are bounded by six choices.
“O(d + V + R) time, O(V) auxiliary space”: Previously explored vectors are not retained.
